items.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021
items.q: I started out playing in that style of Baby Dodds.

ctx.x: When he — he had stock arrangements for a lot of the things that you did. Were there drum parts and were you expected to follow them?

No. I mean there were drum parts, Monk, but if you look at any of those stocks from the 30s, the drum part really, what’s designated for playing time is basically four quarter notes connected by rolls, and four beats on the bass drum. You know that’s kind of a ballpark approximation of what, you know, Baby Dodds would have played or any of the early drummers, you know, that kind of real — nothing on the ride cymbal. There was no ride cymbal. It was all about playing the time on the snare drum. So I started out…
What if someone wanted to do a rumba? Would your father have vocalized the beat to you? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
